subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default policy should OpenClaw apply to externally/plugin/agent-declared recurring cron jobs that would start model-backed background work without an explicit operator action?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix changes compatibility-sensitive cron defaults, plugin scheduling behavior, provider/model selection, cost enforcement, doctor/update UX, and security posture, so automation should not choose the permanent policy unilaterally.

options.title: Design coordinated safe-default cron authority
options.body: Require explicit activation or trusted-source policy for externally declared model-backed recurring jobs, add model/cost preflight and circuit-breaker state, and ship migration/docs/tests together.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical issues
options.body: Keep #41346 as the umbrella but implement consent/defaults, reason-aware cron failures, and gateway spend budgets only after each canonical issue receives a maintainer-approved contract.

options.title: Document trusted-operator behavior and defer
options.body: Keep current default-enabled cron behavior, document the cost/security risk, and rely on manual operator configuration or related future budget work instead of changing core defaults now.

recommendation.title: Design coordinated safe-default cron authority
recommendation.body: Require explicit activation or trusted-source policy for externally declared model-backed recurring jobs, add model/cost preflight and circuit-breaker state, and ship migration/docs/tests together.

likelyOwner.reason: joshavant most recently owned the agent cron caller-scope and Gateway identity plumbing that this policy would build on.
